newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania state budget deficit surges in September.
newsitem.headline: Romania state budget deficit surges in September.

text.p: Romania's state budget deficit widened sharply in September to 2.86 trillion lei for the January-September period from 1.9 trillion lei in the first eight months of this year, official data showed on Tuesday.

Nine-month expenditures stood at 15.41 trillion lei, up from 12.99 trillion at end-August. Revenues rose to 12.55 trillion lei over January-September from 11.09 trillion in the first eight months of 1996.
The state budget deficit is expected to hit 4.27 trillion by the end of the year.

Analysts said the centrist-coalition government emerging from Romania's parliamentary elections this month had to stem the budget deficit to calm inflationary pressure and secure fresh support from international institutions.
The International Monetary Fund suspended loan tranches for Romania this year after expressing concern over foreign exchange market restrictions and on lax budgetary discipline ahead of the election.
The outgoing government has launched several issues of three-month treasury bills to cover the deficit. On Thursday some 155.75 billion lei in 91-day T-bills are on offer.

Last week, an offer of 1.0 trillion lei of three-month T-bills was largely undersubscribed, with five banks buying only 7.98 billion worth of new paper. The remaining bills will be offered in a public subscription on November 22. ($=3,452 lei) -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1-3120264
